How it plays

  1. Three hard-coded rules come first. Win now if it can. Otherwise block a four you could make next move. Avoid a column where its piece would let you win right on top of it.
  2. Everything else is the network. A 84→128→7 MLP (128 hidden ReLU units) scores the seven columns. It was trained in numpy to imitate a depth-7 alpha-beta search.
  3. The stylesheet describes one turn. Each of the 21 turns is a nested element that inherits the board from the turn before it, so the browser reruns the same network for every move.
Every value is an integer custom property below 2²⁴, so each browser plays exactly the move the Python model plays. Digit recognizer · Source on GitHub.
